title: High-temperature superconducting cable for fusion magnets
bottleneck: Fusion pilot plants need toroidal field magnets above 20 T that survive intense neutron flux, huge electromagnetic forces, and thermal cycling. REBCO-based cable-in-conduit conductors exist as prototypes, but no design has demonstrated decades-long reliability under fusion-relevant neutron irradiation, and joint resistances between cable segments remain too high for persistent-mode operation. Radiation damage to the superconductor itself is poorly characterized.
why_it_blocks: Magnet performance sets the size and cost of a fusion plant: stronger fields shrink the machine. Cable and irradiation uncertainties force conservative designs, inflating costs and schedules for every magnetic confinement concept.
current_state: SPARC and other private fusion efforts are procuring REBCO tape at scale, which is driving conductor cost down, but fusion-relevant irradiation testing of full cables is still sparse. The PNAS 2026 agenda flags practical conductors for fusion as a priority application of superconductor research.
